newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bank's net profit seen rising 14.4 pct/97.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bank's net profit seen rising 14.4 pct/97.

text.p: Morocco's Banque Commerciale du Maroc, is expected to show a 14.4 percent rise in its net profit to 705 million dirhams in 1997 compared with 1996, Casablanca-based CFG stockbrokers said.

CFG research department in a newsletter received on Thursday said it expected BCM, which is Morocco's second largest bank, to register strong growth this year and lift net profit up from 615.8 million in 1996.
"Our estimate does not include any capital gain on disposal of assets, contrary to what we believe happened in 1996," CFG said.
Although the 1996 net result had been published the bank's income statement had not been made public yet, brokers said.
The income statement is expected to be released after the shareholders' annual meeting on June 12, 1997.
The bank showed a net profit growth of an average 36 percent between 1993 and 1995, the stockbroking firm said. Growth fell back to 19 percent last year, it said.
CFG said it expected BCM's net banking income to rise to 1.98 billion dirhams in 1997 from 1.73 billion in 1996.
The bank had good risk management and good control of its overheads, it said.
One of the 47 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, BCM closed on Thursday at 775 dirhams, a dealer said.
